    RationsArea 51 green chilli potato chipsPotato chips in salt and green chilli. What the hell is that smell?How to make it600g potatoes2 L vegetable oil1 tsp fine salt1 tsp green chilli powderSlice the potatoes very thin on a mandoline, rinse and dry well.Heat the vegetable oil to 170°C and fry in batches until golden and crisp.Toss with salt and green chilli powder while hot.Fireworks popcornWe will not go quietly into the night! White choc popcorn, popping candyHow to make it100g popcorn kernels150g white chocolate2 tbsp red and blue sprinkles2 packets of popping candyPop the kernels in a covered pot and spread on a lined tray.Melt the white chocolate and drizzle over, tossing gently.Scatter with the sprinkles and popping candy before it sets.Let set, then break into clusters.Russell's crop duster chilli jerkyHe's been ready for them for yearsHow to make itNot on tonight's cookTopside sliced thin and marinated in soy, Worcestershire, brown sugar, chilli and smoked paprika, slow-dried until chewy and smoky.Freeze 800g topside for 1 hour, then slice 3mm thick across the grain.Mix 100ml soy sauce, 2 tbsp Worcestershire, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 2 tsp chilli flakes and 2 tsp smoked paprika.Marinate the beef overnight in the fridge.Pat dry and lay on wire racks over trays.Dry at 70°C with the oven door slightly open for 4 hours until leathery but still bendy.Cool and store airtight.Corn dogs with yellow mustardFourth of July cookout. Welcome to Earth.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.Hot messSmoky pork ribs, corn and potato saladPaprika rubbed ribs baked then glazed, charred corn, Dijon potato saladHow to make it1.5kg pork ribs2 tbsp brown sugar1 tbsp smoked paprika3 garlic cloves, crushed200ml barbecue sauce4 corn cobs1kg potatoes2 tbsp Dijon mustard3 tbsp olive oil2 tbsp white wine vinegarRub the ribs with the brown sugar, paprika and garlic, then wrap tightly in foil.Bake at 150°C until the meat is very tender.Boil the potatoes until tender, cool slightly, and toss with Dijon, oil and vinegar.Unwrap the ribs, brush with barbecue sauce and glaze under a hot grill.Char the corn on a grill.Captain Hiller's cookout cheeseburgersSmashed beef patties and cheese on brioche. He could've been at a barbecue.How to make it800g beef mince, 20% fat8 slices of American cheese4 brioche buns1 iceberg lettuce2 tomatoes1 red onion1 jar dill pickles3 tbsp whole egg mayonnaise1 tbsp American mustard1 tbsp tomato sauce20g butterDivide the mince into 8 balls and keep them cold.Mix the mayonnaise, mustard, tomato sauce and a chopped pickle for the burger sauce. Slice the tomato and onion and shred the lettuce.Butter and toast the buns cut side down.Smash the balls flat on a very hot greased flat plate or pan, season and cook 2 minutes. Flip, top with cheese and cook 1 minute more.Stack two patties on each bun with the sauce, lettuce, tomato, onion and pickles.Sweet issueFlag cakeSponge with cream, berry stars and stripes. We're going to live on!How to make it1 slab sponge cake600ml thickened cream2 tbsp icing sugar125g blueberries500g strawberriesPut the sponge on a board. Whip the cream with the icing sugar to soft peaks and spread over the top.Fill the top left corner with blueberries for the stars.Halve the strawberries and lay rows across for the stripes.CanteenFourth of July bourbon lemonadeBourbon and lemonade over crushed berries. Who's da man?!How to make it5 lemons120ml sugar syrup500ml cold water100g strawberries50g blueberries180ml bourbon1 bunch mint1 bag iceSqueeze four of the lemons, keeping one for wheels, and stir into the syrup and water.Lightly crush the strawberries and blueberries in the bottom of four jars.Fill with ice, add bourbon and top with the lemonade.Stir and garnish with a lemon wheel and mint.Longneck beer on iceRussell picked a hell of a day to quit.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
